papers.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

papers.title: Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
papers.abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{T}_d$ be the triangular lattice with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ the set $\mathcal{T}_d$ can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors, a question left open by Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol for $2-\sqrt3\le d<2/\sqrt{37}$ and on several gaps between their constructions. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points of $\mathcal{T}_d$ in a closed unit disk, we show that $\mathcal{T}_d$ cannot be covered whenever $\mathcal{N}(d)<4/d^2$, and we determine this set of spacings exactly as a union of fifteen intervals; combined with their constructions, this shows that coverability is not monotone in $d$. At the right endpoints $d=2/\sqrt k$ of these intervals the density bound is attained, and we show that such a spacing is coverable if and only if $k$ is the norm of an Eisenstein integer. We also give two new coverings, at $d=1/\sqrt{13}$ and $d=2/\sqrt{21}$, in which the disks form a hexagonal packing. Consequently, together with an earlier result of Okayama, Kiyomi and Uehara, the smallest coverable spacing $d_{\min}$ exists and satisfies $2/\sqrt{55}<d_{\min}\le1/\sqrt{13}$, which answers a question of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol.

papers.title: Integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points in the Heisenberg group
papers.abstract: We investigate the local integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points of surfaces in the first Heisenberg group. We prove that, for every embedded surface of class $C^{2,\alpha}$, with $\alpha>0$, the horizontal mean curvature is locally integrable with respect to (any) Riemannian surface measure, without any assumption on the structure of the characteristic set. We further establish that the horizontal unit normal belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and characterize its $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity in terms of the vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the characteristic set. Finally, we answer an open question by Danielli, Garofalo and Nhieu by constructing a $C^2$ surface with a unique characteristic point whose horizontal mean curvature fails to be locally integrable, thus showing that the additional H\"older regularity cannot, in general, be replaced by $C^2$ regularity.

papers.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.

papers.title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions
papers.abstract: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $\mu$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $\mu(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrectifiable measures with any prescribed exact Hausdorff and packing dimensions $0\leq s_H\leq s_P\leq q$ with $m-1\leq s_P\leq m$, which are doubling when $s_H>0$. This verifies a conjecture of Badger and Schul. The design of the measures relies on metric cubes with variable scaling, in which the ratio of consecutive side lengths tends to infinity but jumps only on a sparse set of generations, together with Badger and Schul's square packing construction of Lipschitz maps.

papers.title: A Weak Topology on Metric Spaces
papers.abstract: We use metric functionals to construct a topology on metric spaces that induces $d$-weak convergence. We show that this topology is invariant under surjective isometries and characterize its convergence in terms of weak metrics. We prove that the topology is $T_1$ on every metric space. For normed linear spaces, we further show that it is Hausdorff and coarser than the classical weak topology. Finally, we construct a sequence in $C[0,1]$ that is unbounded in the sup-norm yet converges $d$-weakly, thereby correcting an assertion in an earlier work.

papers.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
papers.abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.

papers.title: Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces
papers.abstract: We clarify and streamline OpenAI's proof of the sharp Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces. We extend the result to complete spaces without assuming properness or compact support, and we establish rigidity in the equality case.

papers.title: A Topological Approach to the Discrete Dual Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: The discrete dual Minkowski problem asks for the necessary and sufficient conditions on a finite discrete measure $\mu$ on $S^{n-1}$ such that $\mu$ is given by the $q^{th}$ dual curvature measure of a convex polytope in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this paper, using topological degree theory, a novel framework is developed to prove existence of solutions. This approach is applied to the case of polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $q>0$ and $n\geq 2$ whose outer normals are in general position while also subject to a constraint on their distribution on $S^{n-1}$. Moreover, existence of solutions is also proved in the plane under a different constraint on the outer normals by proving that a family of non-linear second-order recurrence relations do not have non-constant $N$-periodic solutions.

papers.title: Convex monohedral tilings: a sharp neighbor bound and rigidity in the equality case
papers.abstract: We study both side-to-side and non-side-to-side convex monohedral tilings of the Euclidean plane in which every tile has the same number of neighbors. Reflections are allowed, point contacts count as neighbors, and no periodicity assumption is imposed. Combining boundary estimates for sums of face curvatures, angle-incidence counts and side-length matching, we prove that the common neighbor number satisfies $N\le21$ and classify all equality cases. Equality holds precisely when the prototile is a $30^\circ$-$30^\circ$-$120^\circ$ triangle and the entire tiling is similar to the central subdivision of the standard equilateral triangular tiling. This resolves the open problem on the maximum common number of neighbors recorded in Adams's The Tiling Book.

papers.title: Triviality of metric fibrations over locally finite metric graphs
papers.abstract: In this note, we give a direct proof that every metric fibration over a geodesic metric space locally modeled on finite metric stars is isometrically isomorphic, over its base, to the $\ell^1$ product of its base and a fiber. Neither compactness nor completeness of the base is assumed. We also construct a nontrivial example over a closed interval with a truncated metric, showing that the local star condition alone does not imply the conclusion.

papers.title: A counterexample to the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture in dimensions three and higher
papers.abstract: Fifteen years after its formulation and following its recent proof in the plane, we show that the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture fails in every dimension $n\geq 3$. For every $n\geq 3$, $r>0$, and $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a compact set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying the interior $r$-sphere condition and containing a point that belongs to no closed ball of radius $(1/2+\varepsilon)r$ contained in $S$. Consequently, the known universal radius $r/2$ is optimal in every dimension $n\geq 3$, even for compact sets, whereas the optimal radius in the plane is $r/\sqrt{3}$. The construction uses simplices with coincident circumcenter and incenter and yields an exact formula for the largest radius of a contained ball covering the center; the regular simplex recovers the original example motivating the conjecture.

papers.title: Branching Pattern Modeling: A Geometric Measure Theory Approach
papers.abstract: This article is based on a lecture given at Westlake University. It aims to introduce students to an application of geometric measure theory in modeling branched patterns found in both living and nonliving systems. We begin with the Eulerian framework of ramified optimal transportation, including discrete transport paths, their basic properties, numerical approximation, and the passage to general transport paths represented by rectifiable currents. We then describe an application to the dynamic formation of a plant leaf, where branching venation patterns arise from a balance between metabolic benefit and transportation cost. Finally, we review landscape functions associated with transport paths and explain how two existing approaches can be unified within a broader family of rectifiable $1$-currents. We conclude by indicating several open directions related to Gilbert-type network problems, biological modeling, and numerical approximation.

papers.title: The Star Geometry of Critic-Based Regularizer Learning
papers.abstract: Variational regularization is a classical technique to solve statistical inference tasks and inverse problems, with modern data-driven approaches parameterizing regularizers via deep neural networks showcasing impressive empirical performance. Recent works along these lines learn task-dependent regularizers. This is done by integrating information about the measurements and ground-truth data in an unsupervised, critic-based loss function, where the regularizer attributes low values to likely data and high values to unlikely data. However, there is little theory about the structure of regularizers learned via this process and how it relates to the two data distributions. To make progress on this challenge, we initiate a study of optimizing critic-based loss functions to learn regularizers over a particular family of regularizers: gauges (or Minkowski functionals) of star-shaped bodies. This family contains regularizers that are commonly employed in practice and shares properties with regularizers parameterized by deep neural networks. We specifically investigate critic-based losses derived from variational representations of statistical distances between probability measures. By leveraging tools from star geometry and dual Brunn-Minkowski theory, we illustrate how these losses can be interpreted as dual mixed volumes that depend on the data distribution. This allows us to derive exact expressions for the optimal regularizer in certain cases. Finally, we identify which neural network architectures give rise to such star body gauges and when do such regularizers have favorable properties for optimization. More broadly, this work highlights how the tools of star geometry can aid in understanding the geometry of unsupervised regularizer learning.

papers.title: Around Sperner's lemma
papers.abstract: Sperner's lemma guarantees a triangle with three different labels. How many such triangles must there be? We begin with the familiar proof by doors and rooms and show that orienting the doors gives an exact signed count. The boundary labeling then provides a lower bound even when the region has holes. With more than three labels, a small geometric construction supplies an additional factor: a boundary that winds $w$ times around a cycle of $n$ labels forces at least $(n-2)|w|$ colorful triangles. We connect the count to Brouwer's fixed point theorem and elementary winding arguments, derive a quantitative version of Tucker's lemma, and conclude with a higher-dimensional glimpse in which the Hopf invariant forces nine tetrahedra.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff and intrinsic flat convergence of RCD(K,N) and Kato spaces
papers.abstract: We consider metric measure spaces $(X,\mathsf{d},\mathscr{H}^N)$ satisfying the curvature-free properties (ETR), (LDB), and whose regular set is almost everywhere quasi-convex. In particular, these assumptions are satisfied by non-collapsed RCD$(K,N)$ spaces without boundary, as well as by non-collapsed strong Kato limit spaces without boundary. In this framework, we establish a local rigidity result for top-dimensional integral currents and deduce uniqueness, up to a sign, of orientations in the sense of metric currents. We then prove stability of orientation under pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and show that, for both the RCD and strong Kato classes, the pointed Gromov--Hausdorff limit coincides with the local intrinsic flat limit. The proof of the convergence is based on the local degree of (ETR) charts and on the $L^1$-stability of the degree under flat convergence. A central ingredient is a full-measure biLipschitz decomposition of splitting charts around almost-Euclidean regular points of non-collapsed RCD$(K,N)$ spaces.

papers.title: Solution of Erd\H{o}s Problem 633
papers.abstract: We classify triangles that can be tiled only into a square number of congruent triangles, settling Erd\H{o}s Problem 633.

papers.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
papers.abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. All the proofs in this paper have been formalized in Lean. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
